ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.claim: Night prayer is the remedy for the anxiety in the address and brings blessings that renew energy and strengthen faith and resolve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r1.anchor: this prayer rejuvenates his energy and strengthens his faith and resolve

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r2.claim: The prayer begins after sleep in the latter half of the night; half the night is especially blessed, with latitude for a little less or more because waking is difficult.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p19/r2.anchor: night refers to the last half of the night when a person gets up after sleeping awhile

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r4.claim: Qatādah says he had wrapped himself for prayer and made ready, so the address means one prepared for worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان تزمل في ثيابه للصلاة واستعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r10.claim: The majority read قم with kasra; Abū al-Sammāl reads it with ḍamma and another reading with fatḥa, since any vowel avoids the meeting of two quiescent consonants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قم الليل، بكسر الميم على أصل التقاء الساكنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r11.claim: Most commentators take the night vigil as recommended, while others say it was obligatory for the Prophet alone or for him and everyone; reports say it lasted a year or two according to Qatādah and eight months according to ʿĀʾishah before 73:20 eased it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r11.anchor: فقال الجمهور: هو على جهة الندب، وقيل: كان فرضا على الرسول خاصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r12.claim: The exception قليلا implies that the command initially covered the whole night; the whole night could not be sustained continuously, so a portion was set aside for rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r12.anchor: وفي قوله: إلا قليلا دليل على أن المستثنى قد يكون مبهم المقدار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r13.claim: The Basrans parse قليلا as an adverb of time, whereas the Kufans parse it as an object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p311/r13.anchor: وهذا عند البصريين منصوب على الظرف، وإن استغرقه الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r1.claim: Wahb b. Munabbih says قليلا means less than one tenth or one sixth; al-Kalbī and Muqātil say it means one third, and another view says less than half.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r1.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: القليل ما دون المعشار والسدس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes half of it as replacing الليل, then excepts a little from that half; he describes a choice between praying a little less than half or varying the amount around half.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نصفه بدل من الليل، وإلا قليلا استثناء من النصف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects making half a replacement for the night because the later instruction to reduce it repeats the earlier exception, an inelegant construction he says is unworthy of the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r3.anchor: فيصير المعنى: قم نصف الليل إلا قليلا، أو انقص من نصف الليل قليلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r4.claim: He also rejects making half a replacement for قليلا: the pronoun then produces either an unintelligible exception from an unknown amount or a needless and confusing exception from the whole night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p312/r4.anchor: لا جائز أن يعود على المبدل منه، لأنه يصير استثناء مجهول من مجهول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers several parses of half as a replacement for قليلا, creating choices among the whole half, an amount just below it, or a greater amount, and other options involving thirds and quarters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وإن شئت جعلت نصفه بدلا من قليلا، وكان تخييرا بين ثلاث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān criticizes al-Zamakhsharī's expansive speculation, insisting that Qurʾānic wording should use the best natural Arabic construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r2.anchor: وما أوسع خيال هذا الرجل، فإنه يجوز ما يقرب وما يبعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah considers قليلا an exception from the act of standing, meaning nights missed for a clear excuse, but Abū Ḥayyān says this is far from the apparent meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وقد يحتمل عندي قوله: إلا قليلا أنه استثناء من القيام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r4.claim: Another view supplies an omitted conjunction and reads the sequence as half, or half, or a third; Abū Ḥayyān objects that the omitted conjunction has no textual indication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p313/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أو نصفه، كما تقول: أعطه درهما درهمين ثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r1.claim: The continuation applies the options of increase and decrease to the last two thirds of the night, with the first third assigned to the evening prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r1.anchor: والنقصان وقع على الثلثين من آخر الليل، لأن الثلث الأول وقت العتمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī offers two condensed analyses of the night-prayer wording, but Abū Ḥayyān directs readers to his longer treatment elsewhere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p314/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: قد أكثر الناس في تفسير هذه الآية

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r1.claim: Rise for the night except for a little of it; half the night is specified, with a minimum quarter and up to three quarters when increasing the portion.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r1.anchor: yarısından az kalk, amma o eksiltmek yarının yarısından yani gecenin dörtte birinden fazla olmasın

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r2.claim: The half, subtraction, and increase may describe either the time spent standing or the small excluded remainder, since either complementary calculation gives the same result.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r2.anchor: Gerek müstesnâ minh gerek müstesnâ hangi taraftan mülâhaza edilse netice aynı olur

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r3.claim: Because subtraction and increase address the addressee's action, they describe the duration of standing; following Abu al-Su'ud, half is an explanatory substitute for the excepted portion of the night.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r3.anchor: Ebussuud’un dediği gibi نِّصْفَهُۥٓ zamîrinin râci‘olduğu müstesnâ minh “leyl”den bedel olarak kıyam müddetini beyan olmak zâhirdir

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r4.claim: The rhetorical wording first follows the usual rule that an exception is smaller, signals that standing more than half is preferable, and treats sleep as little in value compared with worshipful remembrance.
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r4.anchor: Bunda başlıca üç nükte vardır. Birincisi; evvelemirde istisnânın az olması kāidesine tenbih

ELMALILI:73:2-19/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:73:2-19/r5.claim: The three possible portions are offered according to circumstances and the changing length of nights; a quarter is the minimum established as obligatory, while more is recommended.

NAHHAS:v5p55/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p55/r7.claim: The kasra on ميم prevents two sukuns meeting; the واو is not restored because its vowel is not fixed.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r7.anchor: كسرت الميم لالتقاء الساكنين ولم تردد الواو لأن الحركة ليست بلازمة

NAHHAS:v5p55/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p55/r8.claim: One view is that the night prayer was not obligatory; the following option to reduce or increase supports this.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r8.anchor: إن هذا ليس بفرض يدل على ذلك أن بعده

NAHHAS:v5p55/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p55/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that this command was abrogated by the end of the sura.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r9.anchor: والقول الثاني إنه منسوخ نسخة آخر السورة وهذا قول ابن عباس

NAHHAS:v5p55/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p55/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p55/r10.claim: A third view is that the obligation applied to the Prophet alone.
NAHHAS:v5p55/r10.anchor: والقول الثالث إنه كان فرضا فالمخاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r1.claim: The common reading has kasra on م to break the meeting of two quiescent letters; Abu al-Sammal uses damma by vowel harmony with ق, and another reading uses fatha for ease.
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r1.anchor: العامة على كسر الميم لالتقاء الساكنين. وأبو السمال بضمها إتباعا لحركة القاف

SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r2.speaker: أبو الفتح
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r2.claim: Abu al-Fath says any vowel on the first consonant avoids the two quiescent letters; al-Samin maintains kasra is original based on grammarians' evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r2.anchor: الغرض الهرب من التقاء الساكنين، فبأي حركة حرك الأول حصل الغرض

SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r3.claim: Al-Samin favors kasra as the original vowel, following a proof cited by grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r3.anchor: إلا أن الأصل الكسر لدليل ذكره النحويون

SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r4.claim: Basrans treat الليل as a time adverb even though the act of standing spans it; Kufans treat this construction as a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:73:2/r4.anchor: هذا قول البصريين، وإما الكوفيون فيجعلون هذا النوع مفعولا به

ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan except for its last two verses, which are Medinan.
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r1.anchor: (مكية) ما خلا آيتين من آخرها مدنية بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r6.claim: The command means half the night less a little, or less or more than half; “subtract a little” clarifies the range.
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r6.anchor: فالمعنى قم نصف الليل إلا قليلا أو انقص من النصف أو زد على النصف

ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r7.claim: This night-prayer instruction preceded the obligation of the five daily prayers.
ZAJJAJ:v5p239/r7.anchor: وهذا - والله أعلم - قبل أن يقع فرض الصلوات الخمس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says the early Muslims stood at night for a year or two after the command, until their legs and feet swelled; the end of the sūra then brought relief.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى لما نزلت ﴿ قم الليل إلا قليلا ﴾ قاموا حولا أو حولين حتى انتفخت سوقهم وأقدامهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r2.claim: Qatāda concludes that night prayer became voluntary after it had been obligatory.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p324#2/r2.anchor: قال فصار قيام الليل تطوعا بعد فريضة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r1.claim: Qum al-layl can mean rise for prayer or persist in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r1.anchor: أي قم إلى الصلاة وقيل داوم عليها وأيا ما كان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r2.claim: On the first analyses the complement of qum is understood, and al-layl is an adverb of time.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r2.anchor: فمعمول قم مقدر والليل منصوب على الظرفية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r3.claim: Another parse makes al-layl accusative by semantic extension and metaphorical attribution; this is ascribed to the Kufans, with an alternative attribution to the Basrans.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون منصوبا على التوسع والإسناد المجازي ونسب هذا إلى الكوفيين وما قيل إلى البصريين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r4.claim: A further view treats standing as a metaphor for prayer, so qum simply means pray and needs no omitted complement.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r4.anchor: وقيل القيام مستعار للصلاة ومعنى قم صل فلا تقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r5.speaker: أبو السمال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r5.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads the mīm with ḍamma, following the vowel of the qāf.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال بضم الميم اتباعا لحركة القاف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r6.claim: A variant reads the mīm with fatḥa to lighten pronunciation; the majority's kasra follows the original rule at the meeting of two sukūns.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r6.anchor: وقريء بفتحها طلبا للتخفيف والكسر في قراءة الجمهور على أصل التقاء الساكنين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102/r7.claim: The exception of a little is taken from the night.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r5.claim: The author rejects substituting for the excluded little: the phrase's emphasis belongs to the remainder joined to the prayer, not the excluded portion.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p102#3/r5.anchor: وقال في الإبدال من قليل ليس بسديد لهذا ولأن الحقيقي بالإعتناء الذي ينبيء عنه الإبدال هو الجزء الباقي بعد الثنيا المقارن للقيام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r7.claim: One view makes an unrestricted increase complete a third, giving choices of half, a third, or a quarter; the author says its only support is the genitive reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r7.anchor: قيل يجوز أن تجعل الزيادة لكونها مطلقة تتمة للثلث فيكون التخيير بين النصف والثلث والربع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r8.claim: The Imam proposes that little means a third, with half understood after a dropped conjunction, yielding a sequence beginning with two-thirds; the author says this account remains unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r8.anchor: وجوز الإمام أن يراد بقليلا في قوله تعالى إلا قليلا الثلث وقال إن نصفه على حذف حرف العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r9.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil are reported to interpret little as a third.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r9.anchor: نعم تفسيره القليل بالثلث مروي عن الكلبي ومقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r10.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih is reported to interpret little as less than a tenth and a sixth.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r10.anchor: وعن وهب بن منبه تفسيره بما دون المعشار والسدس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r11.claim: This interpretation is cited by those who permit an exception of half or more, a question discussed in legal theory.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r11.anchor: واستدل به من قال بجواز استثناء النصف وما فوقه على ما فصل في الأصول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r12.speaker: التبريزي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r12.claim: Al-Tabrizi says the command targets two-thirds of the final night, since the first third is time for the evening prayer; the exception and half-substitute are construed within that amount.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r12.anchor: وقال التبريزي الأمر بالقيام والتخيير في الزيادة والنقصان وقع على الثلثين من آخر الليل لأن الثلث الأول وقت العتمة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r14.claim: Another view takes the exception from the total number of nights, not their portions, and refers the pronoun to night by semantic reuse for its parts; the author finds it far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r14.anchor: وقيل الإستثناء من أعداد الليل لا من أجزائه فإن تعريفه للإستغراق إذ لا عهد فيه والضمير راجع إليه باعتبار الأجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.claim: After reviewing the many strained constructions, the author prefers his first interpretation as clearest, least contrived, and most fitting to the Qur'an's eloquence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p103/r15.anchor: وأظهر الوجوه عندي وأبعدها عن التكلف وأليقها بجزالة التنزيل هو ما ذكرناه أولا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r4.claim: The command is to rise for night prayer, leaving only a little of the night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r4.anchor: {قم الليل} أي للصلاة {إلا قليلا} وكان قيام الليل فريضة في الابتداء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r6.claim: The Prophet and companions kept the measures; uncertainty about thirds made some stay awake until dawn and their feet swelled, so God relieved them about a year later.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r6.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه يقومون على هذه المقادير، وكان الرجل لا يدري متى ثلث الليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.claim: ʿĀʾishah says the Prophet's character was the Qurʾān and night vigil was obligatory for him and companions for a year until their feet swelled; revelation then made it voluntary.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p246#2/r7.anchor: عن زرارة بن أبي أوفى عن سعيد بن هشام قال: انطلقت إلى عائشة رضي الله عنها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r1.speaker: مقاتل وابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r1.claim: Muqātil and Ibn Kaysān say the night command came in Mecca before the five prayers and was abrogated by them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p250/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل وابن كيسان: كان هذا بمكة قبل أن تفرض الصلوات الخمس، ثم نسخ ذلك بالصلوات الخمس.

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.claim: The command means either rise for prayer or keep up prayer during the night.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.anchor: أي قم إلى الصلاة، أو داوم عليها فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.claim: The mīm is read with ḍamma or fatḥa, for vowel assimilation or ease.
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.anchor: وقرىء بضم الميم وفتحها للإتباع أو التخفيف

BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.claim: The command exempts a small part of the night.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r1.claim: Following the previous sūra's account of revelation and its protection, this sūra prepares the Prophet for prophecy's burdens through intimate night communion, strengthening him for the work among the misguided.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r1.anchor: في آخر الجن من تعظيم الوحي وأن من تعظيمه حفظ المرسل به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r9.claim: Qum calls the Prophet to serve God by bearing prophecy's burdens and exerting himself to carry them; rising requires leaving the wrapping behind.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r9.anchor: أي في خدمتنا بحمل أعباء نبوتنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r10.claim: The whole night stands for a portion of every night; its privacy and concealment suit prayerful communion, and naming prayer signals the other outward and inward works it grounds.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r11.claim: Night standing in Islamic law means prayer; Biqāʿī says it is unqualified here because prayer encompasses the other kinds of outward and inward worship and is their foundation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r11.anchor: وقيام الليل في الشرع معناه الصلاة فلذا لم يقيده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r12.claim: The exception allows the body some rest, while the command still concerns a portion of every night.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r12.anchor: ولما كان للبدن حظ في الراحة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r13.claim: After the first revelation at Ḥirāʾ, the frightened Prophet asked to be wrapped and feared for himself; Khadīja reassured him that God would not disgrace him, citing his care for kin and guests and aid to people in hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r13.anchor: رجع إلى خديجة زوجته رضي الله تعالى عنها يرجف فؤاده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r15.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that after the jinn's acceptance and the failure of apparently more likely hearers to respond, the sūra turns to the Prophet's worship and night remembrances, opening with a gentle address that consoles him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p202/r15.anchor: مفتتحا ذلك بأجمل مكالمة وألطف مخاطبة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r1.claim: Biqāʿī continues Ibn al-Zubayr's coherence reading: Fāṭir 35:8, al-Maʿārij 70:5, al-Muzzammil 73:10–11, and Qāf 50:45 support patience amid opposition, followed by the warning of 73:12.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r1.anchor: وليحصل منه الاكتراث بعناد من قدم عناده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r2.claim: Biqāʿī sees a return to kindness toward the Prophet and companions, despite shortcomings in honoring God; 73:20 acknowledges that they cannot fully measure or fulfill the task and grants relief.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p204/r2.anchor: ثم رجع الكلام إلى التلطف به عليه الصلاة والسلام وبأصحابه

DURR-FULL:v8p322/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet and Muslims stood at night for a full year until their feet swelled; the easing passage made night prayer voluntary after being obligatory, though night prayer should still be observed.
DURR-FULL:v8p322/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم {يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا} قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r4.claim: If the whole sura is Makkan, the command “Stand at night” in 73:2 was given in Mecca.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p252/r4.anchor: يعني وذلك كله بمكة ، أي فتكون السورة كلها مكية فتعين أن قوله : قم الليل } ( المزمل : 2 ) أمر به في مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r2.claim: In another report, people gathered after hearing the Prophet pray; fearing vigil would be prescribed, he left upset. The opening command was treated as obligatory for eight months, then 73:20 lifted it, returning them to the established prayer and removing the extra vigil; al-Tabari transmits it through two lines from Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman from ʿAʾisha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p253/r2.anchor: وهذا ما رواه الطبري بسندين إلى أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة ، وهو يقتضي أن السورة كلها مدنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r1.claim: Qatada, with a similar view from al-Dahhak, takes the Prophet's wrapping literally as preparation for prayer before he was told to rise at night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r1.anchor: وقيل : هو تزمل للاستعداد للصلاة فنودي يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا } وهذا مروي عن قتادة . وقريب منه عن الضحاك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.claim: ʿIkrima reads “wrapped up” metaphorically as taking on the prophetic mission: expend effort in conveying it by night and day, except necessary sleep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة : معناه زملت هذا الأمر فقم به ، يريد أمر النبوءة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r5.claim: قم is intransitive and means pray, unlike قم in 74:2, which means begin the task of warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r5.anchor: وفعل { قم } منزل منزلة اللازم فلا يحتاج إلى تقدير متعلق لأن القيام مراد به الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r6.claim: الليل is an accusative time adverb, the dark period from after ʿisha until dawn; the command covers it except necessary sleep and similar needs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p257/r6.anchor: و { الليل } : زمن الظلمة من بعد العشاء إلى الفجر . وانتصب { الليل } على الظرفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r1.claim: In Qur'anic and Prophetic usage, qiyam al-layl means night prayer apart from Maghrib and ʿIsha and their regular sunnah prayers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r1.anchor: وقيام الليل لقب في اصطلاح القرآن والسنة للصلاة فيه ما عدا صلاتي المغرب والعشاء ورواتبهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r2.claim: The night-prayer command is obligatory for the Prophet alone; Muslims followed his example, and the majority place this before the five daily prayers were prescribed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r2.anchor: وأمر الرسول بقيام الليل أمر إيجاب وهو خاص به لأن الخطاب موجه إليه وحده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r3.claim: Night prayer purifies the Prophet inwardly and prepares him to receive revelation without the strain described when the angel pressed him before 96:1; 73:5 points to this wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r3.anchor: هو أن تزداد به سريرته زكاء يقوي استعداده لتلقي الوحي حتى لا يحرجه الوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r4.speaker: البخاري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r4.claim: A report in al-Bukhari says the angel pressed the Prophet until he was exhausted, then told him to read.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r4.anchor: كما ورد في حديث البخاري : ( فغطني حتى بلغ مني الجهد ) ثم قال : { اقرأ باسم ربك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r5.claim: Because God inspired the Prophet to practice tahannuth in Hira before revelation, the author judges that night prayer was obligatory on him before the five prayers, so he was never without worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r5.anchor: ولهذا نرجح أن قيام الليل فرض عليه قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس عليه وعلى الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r6.claim: The Prophet's obligation continued after the five prayers as a special honor: night was free for intimate devotion, and 17:79 calls it an additional nearness for him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r6.anchor: وقد استمر وجوب قيام الليل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد فرض الصلوات الخمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r7.claim: Night prayer was never obligatory on the rest of the community; they followed the Prophet, who allowed it, and God praised them for it, as in 32:16.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r7.anchor: ولم يكن واجبا على غيره ولم تفرض على المسلمين صلاة قبل الصلوات الخمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r8.claim: ʿAʾisha says night vigil was imposed at the beginning of the sura, so the Prophet and his companions prayed; there is no disagreement that its obligation was lifted from Muslims, leaving it recommended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r8.anchor: قالت عائشة : ( إن الله افترض قيام الليل في أول هذه السورة فقام النبي وأصحابه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.claim: Night prayer is established as recommended for Muslims; scholars disagree whether its obligation continued for the Prophet, a question the author says need not be pursued.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p258/r9.anchor: على أنه لا خلاف في رفع فرض القيام عن المسلمين . وتقرر أنه مندوب فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.claim: The command to remember is coordinated with the night-prayer command, but its unqualified time extends it to night and day, as in 76:25.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p265/r1.anchor: عطف على { قم الليل } ( المزمل : 2 ) وقصد بإطلاق الأمر عن تعيين زمان إلى إفادة تعميمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.claim: The verse shows the Prophet and some companions already prayed at night under the opening command; its “He relented toward you” marks relief for all and abrogates that earlier command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r5.anchor: وصريح هذه الآية ينادي على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقوم من الليل قبل نزول الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.claim: The first command obligated night prayer for the Prophet alone; companions in Mecca followed his example. ʿAʾisha thought the five prayers abrogated a duty on Muslims, but the author calls that an interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p278/r8.anchor: في أن القيام الذي شرع في صدر السورة كان قياما واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r10.speaker: جمهور أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r10.claim: Most scholars hold the command to rise at night was recommended, not obligatory, and was never made a binding duty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r10.anchor: فقال جمهور أهل العلم: هو أمر على جهة الندب مذ كان لم يفرض قط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p386#2/r11.claim: The author supports the recommended reading with the report that the Prophet feared this prayer would become obligatory for the congregation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r1.claim: A sound report says the Prophet led people in Ramadan prayer behind a screen one night; attendance grew, and he stayed away thereafter because he feared the prayer would be prescribed for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r1.anchor: الصحيح أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قام ليلة في رمضان خلف حصير احتجره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r2.claim: One report says the Prophet did not explain his absence from the prayer to the people until after dawn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه لم يكلمهم إلا بعد الصبح.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r3.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r3.claim: Other scholars say night prayer was obligatory when this verse was revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان فرضا في وقت نزول هذه الآية.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r4.claim: One subgroup held it obligatory only for the Prophet, and that it remained so until he died.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كان فرضا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة، وبقي كذلك حتى توفي عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r1.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r1.claim: One view says the obligation was later lifted for the Prophet, so he died with night prayer voluntary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r1.anchor: بل نسخ عنه ولم يمت إلا والقيام تطوع،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r2.claim: Some say night prayer was obligatory for everyone; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says this lasted ten years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: كان فرضا على الجميع ودام الأمر على ما قال سعيد بن جبير عشر سنين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r3.speaker: عائشة وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbās say the universal obligation lasted a year; another report from her says eight months, after which God eased it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r3.anchor: وقالت عائشة وابن عباس دام عاما، وروي عنها أيضا ثمانية أشهر ثم رحمهم الله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the obligation lasted a year or two.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة بقي عاما أو عامين.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r6.speaker: أبو السمال
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Sammāl read qumi al-layl with ḍamma on the mīm; the ordinary kasra is more common in Arabic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال «قم الليل» بضم الميم لاجتماع الساكنين، والكسر في الكلام العرب أكثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r9.claim: He also considers little an exception from the night as a whole, allowing nights missed for a clear excuse; he says this construction especially suits the recommended, rather than obligatory, view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r9.anchor: وقد يحتمل عندي قوله إلا قليلا، أن يكون استثناء من القيام، فيجعل الليل اسم جنس، ثم قال إلا قليلا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says al-Jurjānī's extended and intricate treatment of the verse's construction is mostly unhelpful and incorrect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p387#2/r10.anchor: وقد تكلم الجرجاني رحمه الله في نظمه في هذه الآية بتطويل وتدقيق غير مفيد أكثره غير صحيح.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#2/r1.claim: The command is to stand in prayer at night; night prayer was obligatory for the Prophet except for a little.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى قم الليل أي للصلاة وكان قيام الليل فرضا عليه إلا قليلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r3.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r3.claim: One position says 73:20 abrogated the night-prayer obligation for both the Prophet and his companions; its advocates call this the Quran’s only case of a surah abrogating its own beginning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r3.anchor: فنسخ ذلك عنه وعنهم بقوله تعالى إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل الآية هذا مذهب جماعة من المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r4.claim: Some say the duty was abrogated for the Prophet by the night vigil in 17:79 and for believers by the five daily prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r4.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنه نسخ قيام الليل في حقه بقوله تعالى ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك الإسراء 79

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r5.claim: Another view says night prayer ceased to be obligatory for the community but remained obligatory for the Prophet forever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r5.anchor: وقيل نسخ عن الأمة وبقي عليه فرضه أبدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r6.claim: A further view holds that night prayer was required of the Prophet alone, never of the community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r6.anchor: وقيل إنما كان مفروضا عليه دونهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the initial and final passages of al-Muzzammil were separated by one year.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r7.anchor: أحدهما سنة قال ابن عباس كان بين أول المزمل وآخرها سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r8.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r8.claim: Al-Mawardi transmits the alternative that the initial obligation lasted sixteen months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p388#4/r8.anchor: والثاني ستة عشر شهرا حكاه الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r1.speaker: سعيد بن هشام
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Hisham planned to sell property for horses and weapons and fight the Romans until death; his townsmen recalled that the Prophet had forbidden six men who proposed the same.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r1.anchor: أنه طلق امرأته ثم ارتحل إلى المدينة ليبيع عقارا له بها ويجعله في الكراع والسلاح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r2.claim: Aisha describes the Prophet’s character as the Qur’an, then explains his night vigil in response to Sa'id’s question.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r2.anchor: قالت: فإن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.claim: Aisha reports that night vigil was initially obligatory; the Prophet and companions kept it for a year until their feet swelled, then the surah’s ending eased the duty to voluntary prayer. Ibn Kathir cites Ahmad’s full report and Muslim’s similar version.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r3.anchor: فإن الله افترض قيام الليل في أول هذه السورة، فقام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه حولا حتى انتفخت أقدامهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r4.claim: Aisha describes eight night rak'ahs, sitting for remembrance and supplication at the eighth, then a ninth and two seated rak'ahs after the salutation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r4.anchor: ثم يصلي ثماني ركعات لا يجلس فيهن إلا عند الثامنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r5.claim: As he aged, the Prophet prayed seven plus two seated rak'ahs; when sleep, pain, or illness kept him from night prayer, he prayed twelve by day, and did not recite the whole Qur'an in one night, stay up all night, or fast a full month outside Ramadan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p252/r5.anchor: فلما أسن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخذه اللحم، أوتر بسبع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r1.claim: After hearing Aisha’s account, Ibn Abbas affirmed it and said he would have visited her to hear it directly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r1.anchor: فأتيت ابن عباس فحدثته بحديثها، فقال: صدقت، أما لو كنت أدخل عليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.claim: In another report Aisha says the Prophet came out displeased when people gathered to follow his night prayer, compassionately fearing that the vigil would become obligatory; he urged them to do only what they could sustain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كنت أجعل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصيرا يصلي عليه من الليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r3.claim: Aisha’s report says the people maintained the vigil intensely for eight months, after which God showed mercy, restored the obligatory prayers, and left night prayer voluntary; it also says the best deeds are those done consistently.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says the route through Musa ibn Ubayda is weak, and the sound hadith omits the added claim that this surah was revealed then; the report’s wording may suggest a Medinan surah, but it is Meccan, and its eight-month interval conflicts with Ahmad’s year report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r4.anchor: ورواه ابن أبي حاتم من طريق موسى بن عبيدة الربذي، وهو ضعيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people initially prayed roughly as much at night as in Ramadan, with close to a year between the surah’s beginning and end; several routes likewise report a year.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p253/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: أول ما نزل: أول المزمل، كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في شهر رمضان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says the believers kept night vigil for a year until their feet and shins swelled, then 73:20 brought relief; al-Hasan al-Basri agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن قال: لما نزلت: {يا أيها المزمل}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r2.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet and companions prayed until their feet swelled and that the surah’s ending was held in heaven for sixteen months before it descended.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.claim: Qatada says they kept night vigil for a year or two until their legs and feet swelled, after which God sent relief at the end of the surah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r3.anchor: وقال معمر، عن قتادة: {قم الليل إلا قليلا} قاموا حولا أو حولين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Prophet and a group of companions maintained the commanded vigil for ten years, until the final verse eased it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r4.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد -هو ابن جبير-قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command to the Prophet and believers to rise for most of the night burdened them, then 73:20 relieved and broadened the obligation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p254/r5.anchor: علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.claim: These early authorities say the final verse abrogated the original obligation of night vigil; reports differ on how long that first obligation lasted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p259/r3.anchor: إن هذه الآية نسخت الذي كان الله قد أوجبه على المسلمين

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r9.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r9.claim: The common reading has kasra on mīm to avoid two successive quiescent consonants.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r9.anchor: قراءة العامة: قم بكسر الميم لالتقاء الساكنين

JISHUMI:v10p7131/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r10.speaker: أبو السمال العدوي
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r10.claim: Abu al-Samal al-Adawi reads the mīm with ḍamma to match the ḍamma of qāf.
JISHUMI:v10p7131/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو [السمال] العدوي بضم الميم لأجل ضم القاف

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r1.claim: The command means stop wrapping and sleeping and rise for prayer during the night; the kasra on qum breaks the meeting of two still consonants.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r1.anchor: بكسر الميم لالتقاء الساكنين أي لا تتزمل وترقد ودع هذه الحال لما هو أفضل منها وقم إلى الصلاة في الليل

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r2.claim: Al-layl is accusative as a time adverb with an omitted fī, since the event occurs throughout it; a preposition cannot govern a verb, so the verb-connected accusative is used.

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r3.claim: Some grammarians instead analyze al-layl as a direct object, following its apparent surface use.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قال بعضهم هو مفعول نظرا إلى الظاهر في الاستعمال

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r4.claim: The author compares the construction with witnessing a month and fasting it, warning a day, and reviving Laylat al-Qadr: in each, the time named as object means the worship performed in it.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك فمن شهد منك الشهر فليصمه وقوله لينذر يوم التلاق في أحد الوجهين كما سبق ومثله الإحياء في قوله من أحيى ليلة القدر

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r5.claim: Night runs from sunset until dawn.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r5.anchor: وحد الليل من روب الشمس إلى طلوع الفجر

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r6.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r6.claim: Some knowers say God longed for intimate converse with His beloved and called him to rise in the heart of night; standing and communion taste like paradise, not worldly life.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r6.anchor: قال بعضا لعارفين الله اشتقاق إلى مناجاة حبيبه فناداه أن يقوم فيجوف الليل وقد قالوا إن القيام والمناجاة ليسا من الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r7.claim: The exception of a little is from the night; half of the remaining night is an apposition replacing the whole.
BURSEVI:v10p157#3/r7.anchor: استثناء من الليل {نصفه} بدل من الليل الباقي بعد الثنيا

MUQATIL:73:1-6/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r3.claim: The Prophet was ordered to rise for half the night, with the option to reduce it to a third or increase it to two-thirds.
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r3.anchor: { نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا } [آية: 3] يقول: انقص إلى ثلث الليل { أو زد عليه } يعني على النصف إلى الثلثين

MUQATIL:73:1-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r4.claim: This nighttime-prayer command was given in Mecca before the five daily prayers were instituted.
MUQATIL:73:1-6/r4.anchor: كان هذا بمكة قبل صلوات الخمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r1.claim: “Half of it” is an appositive to “the night”; alternatively, “a little” is excepted from half, meaning pray half the night except a little of that half.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r1.anchor: نصفه ﴾ بدل من الليل والا فليلا استثناء من قوله نصفه تقديره قم نصف الليل إلا قليلا من نصف الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r2.claim: The wāw in inquṣ is read with ḍamma by readers other than ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r2.anchor: بضم الواو غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ قليلا ﴾ إلى الثلث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r3.claim: The decrease from half is to one third.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p290#2/r3.anchor: من النصف بضم الواو غير عاصم وحمزة ﴿ قليلا ﴾ إلى الثلث

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r3.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r3.claim: The common reading gives the mīm of qum a kasra to avoid two adjoining sukūns.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r3.anchor: قراءة العامة بكسر الميم لالتقاء الساكنين

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r4.speaker: أبو السمال
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r4.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads the mīm with ḍamma by following the ḍamma of qāf; fatḥa is also reported for ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r4.anchor: أبو السمال بضم الميم إتباعا لضمة القاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r5.speaker: عثمان بن جني
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r5.claim: Ibn Jinnī says the vowel only serves to make the word pronounceable without two sukūns, so any vowel achieves the purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r5.anchor: قال عثمان بن جني: الغرض بهذه الحركة التبليغ بها هربا من التقاء الساكنين،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r6.claim: Qāma is intransitive and accepts time or place adverbs; a place adverb needs a preposition, as in standing in or outside a house.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r6.anchor: وهو من الأفعال القاصرة غير المتعدية إلى مفعول، فأما ظرف الزمان والمكان فسائغ فيه،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r7.claim: It is also said that qum here means pray, a metaphor that became conventional through frequent use.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r7.anchor: وقد قيل: إن «قم» هنا معناه صل عبر به عنه واستعير له حتى صار عرفا بكثرة الاستعمال.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.claim: Night extends from sunset until dawn; al-Qurṭubī says its definition was explained earlier in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r8.anchor: حد الليل: من غروب الشمس إلى طلوع الفجر. وقد تقدم بيانه في سورة «البقرة»

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.claim: Scholars disputed whether night prayer was obligatory or recommended; al-Qurṭubī considers obligation stronger, since a recommendation would not single out part of the night without a fixed time, and reports from ʿĀʾisha support it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r9.anchor: والدلائل تقوى أن قيامه كان حتما وفرضا وذلك أن الندب والحض لا يقع على بعض الليل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the obligation addressed the Prophet alone, because the command is directed specifically to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r10.anchor: الأول قول سعيد بن جبير لتوجه الخطاب إليه خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says night prayer was obligatory for Muhammad and the prophets before him.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r11.anchor: الثاني قول ابن عباس، قال: كان قيام الليل فريضة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى الأنبياء قبله.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r12.speaker: عائشة وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r12.claim: ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbās say it was obligatory for the Prophet and his community; al-Qurṭubī calls this the correct view and cites the Muslim report continued in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-2/r12.anchor: الثالث قول عائشة وابن عباس أيضا وهو الصحيح كما في صحيح مسلم عن زرارة بن أوفى

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r1.claim: In the report of Saʿd ibn Hishām, ʿĀʾisha says night prayer was imposed at the start of the sūra; the Prophet and Companions kept it for a year, then the closing verses brought relief and it became voluntary after an obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r1.anchor: فقلت لعائشة: أنبئيني عن قيام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ فقالت: ألست تقرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after the opening verses were revealed, the Companions stood for prayer about as long as they did in Ramadan until the ending came roughly a year later.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r2.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول لما أنزل أول { يأيها المزمل } كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r4.claim: The exception is from the night: pray nearly all night, leaving a little for bodily rest because continually standing through the whole night is impossible.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r4.anchor: استثناء من الليل، أي صل الليل كله إلا يسيرا منه لأن قيام جميعه على الدوام غير ممكن،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī defines a little as less than half, while reporting narrower estimates from Wahb and from al-Kalbī and Muqātil.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r5.anchor: والقليل من الشيء ما دون النصف فحكي عن وهب بن منبه

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r6.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih estimates the little portion as less than a tenth and a sixth.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r6.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه أنه قال: القليل ما دون المعشار والسدس.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r7.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-3/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil identify the little portion as one third.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r1.claim: A Muslim report from Abū Hurayra says God calls to supplicants, petitioners, and those seeking forgiveness after the first third of night passes, continuing until dawn; the parallel report with Abū Saʿīd encourages praying two-thirds of the night.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r1.anchor: ينزل الله عز وجل إلى سماء الدنيا كل ليلة حين يمضي ثلث الليل الأول، فيقول أنا الملك أنا الملك

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r2.claim: Another Muslim report from Abū Hurayra, transmitted by two routes with uncertainty, places the descent after half the night or two-thirds of it.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r2.anchor: إذا مضى شطر الليل أو ثلثاه ينزل الله

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة وأبو سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r3.claim: The Nasaʾī report says a caller is sent after the first half of night to invite prayer, forgiveness, and requests; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq authenticated it, and al-Qurṭubī says it clarifies that the descent is at midnight.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r3.anchor: أبي هريرة وأبي سعيد رضي الله عنهما قالا: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله عز وجل يمهل حتى يمضي شطر الليل الأول،

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r4.claim: Ibn Mājah’s report from Abū Hurayra places the Lord’s descent when the last third remains and describes calls for anyone who asks, invokes, or seeks forgiveness until dawn.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ينزل ربنا تبارك وتعالى حين يبقى ثلث الليل الآخر

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r5.claim: The reports led people to prefer prayer at the end of the night over prayer at its beginning.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r5.anchor: فكانوا يستحبون صلاة آخر الليل على أوله

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r6.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r6.claim: Al-Qurṭubī’s scholars say the order of the reports aligns with the Qurʾān, since both illuminate from one source.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r6.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وبهذا الترتيب انتظم الحديث والقرآن، فإنهما يبصران من مشكاة واحدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts staying with Maymūna: around midnight, give or take a little, the Prophet awoke and made a light ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r7.anchor: من حديث ابن عباس: " بت عند خالتي ميمونة حتى إذا انتصف الليل أو قبله بقليل

QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿĀʾisha identify the closing verse 20 as the abrogation of the night-prayer command.
QURTUBI-FULL:73:1-4/r8.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وعائشة أن الناسخ للأمر بقيام الليل قوله تعالى:

QASHANI:73:1-4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:73:1-4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:73:1-4/r2.claim: Rise from heedlessness, travel God’s path through the wilderness of the lower soul and the heart’s stages, and journey to God.
QASHANI:73:1-4/r2.anchor: سالكا مسالك بيداء النفس ومراحل مفازة القلب إلى الله

QASHANI:73:1-4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:73:1-4/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:73:1-4/r3.claim: The small exception allows necessary rest, food, drink, and bodily needs; together these occupy half the time spent in the natural station, a quarter of the full day each.
QASHANI:73:1-4/r3.anchor: بحكم الضرورة للاستراحة والأكل والشرب ومصالح البدن ومهماته

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that night vigil was initially obligatory for the Prophet because the command's apparent sense is obligation, but was later abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : إن قيام الليل كان فريضة على رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.claim: One account says the night-vigil duty was imposed before the five prayers and then abrogated by them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r2.anchor: أنه كان فرضا قبل أن تفرض الصلوات الخمس ثم نسخ بها

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.claim: In another account, uncertainty about the required portion made people pray all night; their feet and shins swelled and the hardship was relieved by 73:20 in early Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r3.anchor: فكان الرجل لا يدري كم صلى وكم بقي من الليل فكان يقوم الليل كله

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the initial requirement lasted one year; another narration places its imposition in Mecca and abrogation in Medina, followed by abrogation through the five prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r4.anchor: ثم قال ابن عباس : وكان بين أول هذا الإيجاب وبين نسخه سنة

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.claim: Some scholars deny that tahajjud was ever obligatory, citing 17:79, which calls it a supererogatory addition for the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : التهجد ما كان واجبا قط

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas answers that nafilah in 17:79 means an additional obligation for the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r6.anchor: وأجاب ابن عباس عنه بأن المعنى زيادة وجوب عليك

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.claim: A second argument against obligation says that a Prophet's duty would bind his community through the command to follow him, and abrogation conflicts with the default rule.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : التهجد ما كان واجبا قط

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r9.claim: Those denying obligation argue that the imperative means recommendation: Qur'anic commands sometimes oblige and sometimes recommend, so its shared sense is preference for action over omission.

RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.speaker: القائلون بعدم الوجوب
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.claim: They add that permissibility of omission follows from the default; combined with the command's preference for action, this yields a recommended act.
RAZI-FULL:v30p151#2/r10.anchor: فلما حصل الرجحان بمقتضى الأمر وحصل جواز الترك بمقتضى الأصل

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r1.speaker: أبو السمال
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r1.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads the mīm in qum al-layl with fatḥ; other readers use ḍamm.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو السمال { قم اليل } بفتح الميم وغيره بضم الميم

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r2.speaker: ابن جني
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni says the vowel avoids two successive sukūns, and any vowel achieves that purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جني : الغرض من هذه الحركة الهرب من التقاء الساكنين

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r3.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r3.claim: Qutrub reports analogous forms in qum al-layl, qul al-haqq, and biʿ al-thawb: kasra follows the base, ḍamm follows the next sound, and fatḥ favors ease.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r3.anchor: وحكى قطرب عنهم : قم الليل ، وقل الحق برفع الميم واللام وبع الثوب

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r4.claim: First of two readings: little means one third, since 73:20 shows two thirds as the highest amount and thus permits sleeping one third; the command is to rise for two thirds.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r4.anchor: أن المراد بقوله : { إلا قليلا } الثلث

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r6.claim: Under the first reading, one third is the required minimum, two thirds the maximum, and any amount above one third is recommended.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r6.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون الثلثان أقصى الزيادة ، ويكون الثلث أقصى النقصان

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r9.claim: Second reading: half glosses little because it is little relative to the whole; if half is required, a slight extra is needed to ensure fulfillment.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r9.anchor: أن نصف الشيء قليل بالنسبة إلى كله

RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r10.claim: On the second reading, the options are half the night, one quarter, or three quarters; one quarter is obligatory and any increase is recommended, resolving the objection from 73:20.
RAZI-FULL:v30p152/r10.anchor: يعني أو انقص من هذا النصف نصفه حتى يبقى الربع

STUDYQURAN:73:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r5.claim: Before the five daily prayers, night vigil was common for the Prophet and his small group of followers, who reportedly prayed until their feet swelled.
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r5.anchor: Before the five daily prayers were revealed, night vigil was the common practice of the Prophet and his small group of followers, who would reportedly stand in prayer until their feet swelled.

STUDYQURAN:73:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r6.claim: The practice was eased in verse 20 and explicitly made supererogatory in 17:79.
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r6.anchor: The practice was then eased in v. 20 and was made explicitly supererogatory in 17:79

STUDYQURAN:73:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r7.speaker: a famous ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r7.claim: A famous report says that in the night’s last third God descends to the lowest heaven and calls for people to invoke, ask, or seek forgiveness so that He may respond, give, or forgive.
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r7.anchor: a famous ḥadīth says, “Every night during the last third of the night, our Lord descends to the Heaven of this earth

STUDYQURAN:73:1/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r8.claim: The Quran presents night vigil as a supererogatory practice of the upright among the People of the Book and cites it in several other passages.
STUDYQURAN:73:1/r8.anchor: Night vigil is also a supererogatory practice that the Quran attributes to the upright among the People of the Book

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r1.claim: All events happen through God: gnostics know, the spirits of the truthful find intimacy, monotheists' understanding stands before divine majesty, worshippers admit they cannot deserve worship, and all confess they cannot know God's grandeur.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r1.anchor: الحادثات بالله حصلت ، فقلوب العارفين بالله عرفت ما عرفت وأرواح الصديقين بالله ألفت من ألفت وفهوم الموحدين بساحات جلاله وقفت

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.claim: Night vigil was initially obligatory, with the Prophet allowed to pray approximately one-third to one-half of the night or somewhat more; after the five prayers became obligatory it was abrogated for the community but remained obligatory for him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r4.anchor: قم نصف الليل ، وأنقص من النصف

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r5.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r5.claim: A Sufi address calls Muhammad to rise at night under the burdens of prophethood.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r5.anchor: ويقال : يا أيها المتزمل بأعباء النبوة

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r6.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r6.claim: Another address tells the one concealing what God specially granted him to rise, warn, and trust in divine support.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r6.anchor: ويقال : يا أيها الذي يخفي ما خصصناه به قم فأنذر . . فإنا نصرناك

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r7.claim: Another address says that while all others rest at night, the one appointed by God should rise for Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r7.anchor: ويقالك قم بنا . . يا من جعلنا الليل ليسكن فيه كل الناس . . قم أنت

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r8.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r8.claim: One explanation says God speaks of Himself in commanding the Prophet's night vigil for the community, honoring his rank and capacity.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r8.anchor: ويقال : لما فرض عليه القيام بالليل أخبر عن نفسه لأجل أمته إكراما لشأنه وقدرة

QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r9.claim: A report says God descends each night to the lowest heaven; Qushayrī leaves uncertain whether the report's interpretation is known, while lovers have abundant comforts and gifts before that question is resolved.
QUSHAYRI:v3p359/r9.anchor: وفي الخبر : ( أنه ينزل كل ليلة إلى السماء الدنيا . . . ) ولا يدرى التأويل للخبر ، أو أن التأويل معلوم

TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the Prophet was described as wrapped in his clothes and preparing for prayer.
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] أي المتزمل في ثيابه

TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r3.claim: Ikrima interprets the wrapping figuratively: Muhammad took on the matter of prophecy and was told to rise to it.
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا} [المزمل: 2] قال: زملت هذا الأمر فقم به

TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Qatada's literal reading: the following command to rise at night explains that the Prophet was wrapped in garments for prayer, the more apparent of the two senses.
TAB-FULL:v23p357#2/r4.anchor: والذي هو أولى القولين بتأويل ذلك، ما قاله قتادة لأنه قد عقبه بقوله: {قم الليل} [المزمل: 2]

TAB-FULL:v23p358/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to rise for the whole night except a little; the following directions specify half the night, or a little less or more, as God gave him latitude when night prayer was prescribed.
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r1.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس، يقول: لما نزل أول المزمل، كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في رمضان

TAB-FULL:v23p358/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the opening of the sura was revealed, they kept night prayer at about the measure of their Ramadan prayers; nearly a year passed between its beginning and end.
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r2.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس، يقول: لما نزل أول المزمل، كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في رمضان

TAB-FULL:v23p358/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r3.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r3.claim: Aisha reports that people gathered after hearing the Prophet pray on a mat; he feared the prayer would be prescribed, urged manageable and lasting good works, and night prayer was imposed before later being eased after eight months.
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r3.anchor: عن عائشة، قالت: كنت أجعل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصيرا يصلي عليه من الليل

TAB-FULL:v23p358/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r4.claim: A second Aisha version says the Prophet feared making the gathering's night prayer obligatory; it was prescribed like an obligation, then eased by 73:20, removing its obligatory status while leaving voluntary night prayer.
TAB-FULL:v23p358/r4.anchor: عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، عن عائشة قالت: كنت أشتري لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصيرا

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command to the Prophet and believers to pray most of the night was difficult, then 73:20 eased it by allowing whatever recitation was manageable.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {قم الليل إلا قليلا نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا أو زد عليه ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} [المزمل: 3]

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.claim: Saʿid reports that the Prophet and some Companions maintained the commanded night vigil for ten years, until the final passage of the sura lightened the duty.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r2.anchor: عن سعيد، قال: لما أنزل الله على نبيه: {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] قال: مكث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan say the night-prayer command was abrogated by the verse saying God knew they could not keep its measure and permitted easy recitation.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة والحسن، قالا: قال في سورة المزمل {قم الليل إلا قليلا نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.claim: Qatada says they kept the night vigil for a year or two, until their shins and feet swelled; relief came at the end of the sura.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {قم الليل إلا قليلا} [المزمل: 2] قاموا حولا أو حولين حتى انتفخت سوقهم

TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reports that people prayed for a year until swollen feet and shins were relieved when 73:20 instructed them to recite what was manageable.
TAB-FULL:v23p361/r5.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن، قال: لما نزلت: {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] قاموا بها حولا حتى ورمت

TAB-FULL:v23p362/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to stand for the whole night except a little of it.
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قال لما نزلت {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] الآية، قام المسلمون حولا، فمنهم من أطاقه

TAB-FULL:v23p362/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Muslims kept night vigil for a year after the opening of the sura; some could sustain it and some could not, until the concession came.
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، قال لما نزلت {يا أيها المزمل} [المزمل: 1] الآية، قام المسلمون حولا، فمنهم من أطاقه

TAB-FULL:v23p362/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the first verses of al-Muzzammil led them to stand for roughly the same amount as Ramadan night prayer, and about a year separated the sura's beginning from its ending.
TAB-FULL:v23p362/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لما نزل أول المزمل كانوا يقومون نحوا من قيامهم في شهر رمضان، وكان بين أولها وآخرها نحو من سنة

TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says night prayer was first obligatory, then God eased and removed that obligation for the Prophet and community; the later night vigil is voluntary for Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v23p376/r6.anchor: وهذا حين كانت صلاة الليل فريضة، ثم إن الله من على العباد فخففها ووضعها

TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.claim: Qatada reports that night prayer was imposed at the sura's beginning; Muhammad and his Companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, then after twelve months the easing made it voluntary after having been obligatory.
TAB-FULL:v23p397/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: ثم أنبأ بخصال المؤمنين، فقال: {علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.claim: The sura commands the Prophet to pray at night to prepare for the weighty revelation, endure opponents' abuse, and leave them graciously; it warns unbelievers, extends the ruling to believers, then eases it.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r1.anchor: تأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بقيام الليل والصلاة فيه ليستعد بذلك لتلقي ثقل ما سيلقى عليه من القول الثقيل

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.claim: The sura is Meccan and among the earliest revelations; it is said to be the second or third sura revealed.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r2.anchor: والسورة مكية من عتائق السور النازلة في أول البعثة

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r6.claim: As in 2:45, prayer and patience are means to resist severe distress; the Prophet is directed to them instead of wrapping himself up to sleep.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r6.anchor: فأفيد بذلك أن عليه أن يقاوم الكرب العظام والنوائب المرة بالصلاة والصبر لا بالتزمل والنوم

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r9.claim: Standing the night means rising during it for prayer; al-layl functions as an object by broad usage, as in saying one entered the house.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r9.anchor: المراد بقيام الليل القيام فيه إلى الصلاة فالليل مفعول به توسعا كما في قولهم دخلت الدار

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r10.claim: Another parsing supplies an implied destination after qom and makes al-layl an adverb: rise for prayer at night.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r10.anchor: والتقدير قم إلى الصلاة في الليل

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r11.claim: The exception illa qalilan is taken from the night.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r11.anchor: وقوله { إلا قليلا } استثناء من الليل

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r12.claim: The preferred parsing makes half a substitute for the night-except-a-little phrase; its pronouns refer to the half and night, offering a choice of half, slightly less, or slightly more.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r12.anchor: ظاهر السياق أنه بدل من { الليل إلا قليلا } المتعلق به تكليف القيام

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r13.claim: An alternative makes half a substitute for the excepted little: stand all but half, or a little more or less than half.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r13.anchor: وقيل { نصفه } بدل من المستثنى أعني { قليلا } فيكون المعنى قم الليل إلا نصفه

TABATABAI:73:1-4/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r14.claim: Though both parsings yield the same result, the first comes sooner to mind because clarifying the ruling's object precedes clarifying its attached details.
TABATABAI:73:1-4/r14.anchor: والوجهان وإن اتحدا في النتيجة غير أن الوجه السابق أسبق إلى الذهن

TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.claim: The tartil clause coordinates with the command to stand: stand at night and recite the Quran distinctly.
TABATABAI:73:4-5/r4.anchor: أي قم الليل واقرأ القرآن بترتيل

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.claim: Commentators disagree whether the original night command meant prayer or Quran recitation outside prayer.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r11.anchor: وللقوم في كون المراد بقيام الليل الصلاة فيه أو قراءة القرآن خارج الصلاة

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.claim: One reported legal view makes night vigil obligatory for both the Prophet and believers.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r12.anchor: في كونه واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمؤمنين

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r13.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r13.claim: Another reported view recommends night vigil for everyone.

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.claim: A third view makes it obligatory for the Prophet and recommended for others.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r14.anchor: أو واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مستحبا لغيره

TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.claim: Commentators also disagree whether the easing abrogated the earlier ruling or changed the commanded prayer into reciting what is manageable.
TABATABAI:73:20#2/r15.anchor: ثم في نسخ الحكم بالتخفيف بما تيسر بهذه الآية أو تبديل الصلاة من قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن أقوال

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.claim: The Abu Ja'far report presents the sura's opening as requiring night prayer and its ending as abrogating that duty; al-Tabataba'i says his preceding discussion addresses this view.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r1.anchor: أقول محصل الرواية أن صدر السورة توجب صلاة الليل وذيلها تنسخها

TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.claim: Similar reports through Sunni routes from Ibn Abbas and others also describe abrogation of the opening night-prayer command.
TABATABAI:73:20#4/r2.anchor: وروي ما يقرب منه من طرق أهل السنة عن ابن عباس وغيره

AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p552/r2.claim: The sense inserts an omitted أو before نصفه: or half the night, or a little less, or more; Arabic can omit أو in such a sequence, as in giving one, two, or three dirhams.
